subject: maths
title: Polar Form and De Moivre's Theorem
welcome_lead: Switch to polar form and use De Moivre to power and root complex numbers.
meta_desc: HL Maths adventure on polar form r(cosθ + i sinθ) and De Moivre's theorem.
final_note: De Moivre: powers raise the modulus and multiply the angle!

concepts.def: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ).
z = r e^(iθ), via Euler's formula.
(cos θ + i sin θ)^n = cos(nθ) + i sin(nθ).

mcqs.q: De Moivre: (cos θ + i sin θ)^n =?
options: n cos θ + n i sin θ

free_texts.q: Whose theorem powers polar complex numbers?
